newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary rains trigger wheat futures price rise.
newsitem.headline: Hungary rains trigger wheat futures price rise.

text.p: Milling wheat futures rose on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Tuesday on fears of low-quality crops, traders said.
"Dealers...were afraid the rains could endanger the quality of the wheat crop," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
He added, however, that the rise was unlikely to last for long and he predicted a downward correction once the weather started to improve.
Milling wheat futures rose by between 40 and 370 forints per tonne for all but the steady August maturity in relatively light turnover.
Showers and cold weather hit Hungary over the weekend but forecasters said conditions were likely to change by the second half of the week.
Meteorologists said the amount of precipitation was beneficial for the wheat crop.
Maize futures remained flat for all but November and March, which dropped 70 and 50 forints to 18,500 and 20,000, respectively.
September barley dropped 300 forints to 17,500 while May rose 400 to 20,900, but Szoke said the price movements were not indicative of any trend as they happened in low-volume, last-minute deals.
Total grains turnover remained below average at 723 lots, or 287.7 million forints, compared with Monday's 674 lots, or 270 million forints.
Szoke said turnover was likely to pick up if the weather improved.
